SK2091 An exception is thrown from a finally block

A throw written inside a finally replaces whatever exception was already in flight.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0
SupersedesS1163

Why

A finally runs while an exception is unwinding, and a throw from it does not join that exception — it replaces it. The failure that explains everything is destroyed, and the log is left holding the cleanup's complaint about a state the original failure created. The report names the one failure nobody can diagnose from, which is why this is worth a rule rather than a review comment.

Example

Instead of:

try {
    Import(path);
} finally {
    if (!_committed) {
        throw new InvalidOperationException("the import did not commit");
    }
}

Write:

try {
    Import(path);
} finally {
    if (!_committed) {
        _log.LogWarning("the import did not commit");
    }
}

When it does not fire

⚠ Only an explicit `throw`. A finally that calls a method which might throw is every finally ever written — Dispose, Close and Flush all can — so a rule asking "can anything in here throw" would fire across the whole tree and be switched off within a day. The keyword written inside the block is the author's own statement of intent and is the only thing the rule reads. A throw inside the try block of a nested try/catch within the finally never leaves it and is not reported, and neither is one held by a lambda or a local function, which may never be invoked. Nested finally blocks report against the innermost one that owns the keyword, so one throw produces one finding rather than one per enclosing clause. Report-only: deleting the throw discards whatever it was reporting and moving it out of the finally changes when it runs, and which of those the author meant is not visible in the block.
